author: Benoit Dubeau
description: From chips and power to applications

sources.title: How microchips are made. Undated.
sources.note: Manufacturing overview and types of chipmakers. Supports fabrication and lithography basics, not current supply availability.

sources.title: Advanced Packaging Services. Undated.
sources.note: 3DFabric and integration descriptions. Manufacturer explanation of packaging; no market-share or performance claim adopted.

sources.title: GPU Performance Background User’s Guide. Technical reference.
sources.note: Sections 2–4, architecture, execution and performance. Supports parallel calculation and memory limits; older product benchmark numbers are excluded.

sources.title: Understanding Your Grace-Blackwell Systems. Undated technical documentation.
sources.note: System architecture and networking. One documented platform, not a universal hardware layout.

sources.title: Rubin platform announcement. 5 January 2026.
sources.note: Vera Rubin NVL72 composition: 72 GPUs and 36 CPUs. Announced manufacturer specification, not evidence of deployment or independent performance.

sources.title: Hotter Than a Hot Tub. 21 June 2026.
sources.note: Cooling loops and climate qualifications. Vendor account; no promotional water, cost or efficiency ratios adopted.

sources.title: Key Questions on Energy and AI. 2026.
sources.note: Executive summary, demand outlook and value-chain constraints. 485 TWh is the 2025 global data center estimate; 950 TWh is the 2030 central projection. Includes non-AI workloads. Does not identify a particular site’s limiting factor.

sources.title: What is Amazon EC2. Undated technical documentation.
sources.note: Instances and resource configurations. Illustrates infrastructure access, not a comparison of cloud providers.

sources.title: Real-time inference. Undated technical documentation.
sources.note: Managed hosting endpoints and autoscaling. Supports the division of responsibilities; no pricing or service-performance claim adopted.

sources.title: Introduction to Large Language Models. Updated 9 January 2026.
sources.note: Introductory definitions of language models, tokens and parameters. Conceptual reference, not evidence of model quality.

sources.title: LLMs What is a large language model. Technical lesson.
sources.note: Architecture, training, generation and limitations. The article uses broad concepts without treating the lesson’s full-transformer example as universal.

sources.title: Retrieve data and generate AI responses with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. Undated technical documentation.
sources.note: Retrieval, context augmentation and references. Documents features, not a guarantee of answer accuracy.

sources.title: Best Practices Guide for Energy-Efficient Data Center Design. Revised July 2024.
sources.note: Sections 5.1–5.6, 6 and 8, including evaporative and dry heat rejection, climate conditions, electrical systems and benchmarking. Rechecked 5 October 2026; no current numerical benchmarks adopted.

sources.title: Building effective agents. 19 December 2024.
sources.note: Distinguishes predefined workflows from model-directed tool use. Used for a stable architectural distinction, not current product capabilities.

sources.title: Code generation. Live technical documentation, accessed 5 October 2026.
sources.note: Describes Codex as a coding agent and distinguishes it from models integrated into applications. No performance or pricing claim adopted.

sources.title: Enabling Claude Code to work more autonomously. 29 September 2025.
sources.note: Describes coding tools, context management and permissions around the model. Supports the product architecture; the discussion of future interfaces and outcome-based pricing is an open question, not a vendor forecast.
